content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Erika Bolton (E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (from HR presumably): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says admin only if role owns system; Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist; Analyst max write.
- Note 2 (from Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security DB shows contractor with basic training; max read for Payroll; requested admin, grant read.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor.

The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → read max.

Full-time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so max write.

The decision hinges on employment type. Conflicting facts. As Approver, I need to decide. Typically in these tasks, Security DB is considered authoritative over HR note (the security note explicitly says "Security DB shows contractor"). So the employee is contractor with basic training, max read. Requested admin → grant read.

So submit decision: read.
